## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A one-fascicle late-tenth-century Sòng-period translation by **Dānapāla** ([施護](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%96%BD%E8%AD%B7), fl. 980–1017) of an alternative recension of the **Jewel-Casket-Seal Dhāraṇī** family (cf. [KR6j0215](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0215)–[KR6j0216](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0216) = Amoghavajra's eighth-century version). Dānapāla's translation is the principal Northern-Sòng recension and represents an independent Indic transmission, presumably from the manuscript collection that the Sòng-court translation institute (傳法院) had assembled in Chángān after 980.

**Abstract**

Dānapāla was one of the three principal Northern-Sòng court translators (along with [天息災](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%A4%A9%E6%81%AF%E7%81%BD) Tiānxīzāi / [法賢](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E8%B3%A2) Fǎxián and [法天](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E5%A4%A9) Fǎtiān) at the **Yìjīng yuàn** 譯經院 founded by [宋太宗](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AE%8B%E5%A4%AA%E5%AE%97) Sòng Tàizōng in 980. Together they produced the bulk of the Northern-Sòng translation programme — the last great wave of Indic-to-Chinese Buddhist translation. The present *Bǎoqièyìn xīn tuóluóní* recension supplements Amoghavajra's eighth-century version with a freshly-translated Indic source-text; the new recension was needed because the Sòng court was engaged in a systematic re-evaluation of dhāraṇī-orthography against contemporary Sanskrit-language sources (the **Siddham** Sanskrit script was newly available in Sòng China through the Yìjīng yuàn). The recension differs from Amoghavajra's principally in the dhāraṇī orthography and a slightly elaborated narrative-frame; the doctrinal content (dhāraṇī = Tathāgata's *quánshēn shèlì* / "whole-body relic") is preserved.
